article:
Most products do not need a login yet

An account is how you recognise someone next time. It is also passwords, email, reset links, sessions, abuse. If the product works without knowing who they are, ship it without knowing who they are.

This site lets anyone leave a mark. Only I can tend the tape. That is two kinds of “who” and neither of them is a full user system.

When you do need one

When the person has something that is theirs — an order history, a paid workspace, a mailbox. Then you still should not invent passwords. Use a provider: Sign in with X, Google, Apple, or a hosted auth like Supabase Auth. They have already lost those fights for you.

A session is a stamp that says “this browser is that person, for a while.” When it expires they sign in again. That is enough mental model.

How I actually do it

Send Reorder has to know the shop. That identity comes from Shopify, not from a form I designed at midnight. Meeting Mode, if it listens, has to know whose meeting it is. I would rather borrow that from the calendar than mint a new password.

Where noobs get stuck

A signup screen on a site with one visitor. Rolling their own JWT tutorial. Storing passwords in plain text because the model wrote it that way and nobody read the file.

Film this

Two doors: “anyone can talk” and “only I can edit.” Show the edit-key prompt. Then say what would have to be true before a stranger gets an account.

Do this before chapter 12

  • Write who the product must recognise, if anyone.
  • If the answer is “me,” an edit key is enough.
  • If the answer is “customers,” pick a provider. Do not start a password form.

Next: payments — a test card, then one real pound.
